hints.content:
We know the function is a result of translations and stretches applied on the basic function $\cos(x)$, because $h(x)$ is of the form $a\cos(bx+c)+d$.

The basic function $\cos(x)$ has a maximum point at $(0,1)$, its period is $2\pi$ units, and its amplitude is $1$ unit.

$\qquad$[[☃ image 1]]

Let's transform the graph of $\pink{\cos(x)}$ into the graph of $h(x)$ step by step and see how the formula changes along the way.

options.alt: A graph of a trigonometric wave on an x y coordinate plane. The x and y axes scale by one. The maximum parts of the graph are at (negative two pi, one), (zero, one), and (two pi, one). The minimum parts of the graph are at (pi, negative one), (negative pi, negative one), (three pi, negative one), and (negative three pi, negative one). There is a point at (zero, one) and at (pi, negative one).

hints.content:
$h$'s period is equal to twice the horizontal distance between the highlighted points, which is $2\cdot\dfrac{3\pi}{2}=\blue{3\pi}$ units. In order to horizontally stretch the period of $\cos(x)$ to $3\pi$ units, we need to multiply $x$ by $\dfrac{2\pi}{\blue{3\pi}}=\dfrac{2}{3}$ to obtain $\cos\left(\dfrac{2}{3} x\right)$.

$h$'s amplitude is equal to half the vertical distance between the highlighted points, which is $\dfrac{7}{2}=3.5$ units. In order to vertically stretch the amplitude of $\cos\left(\dfrac{2}{3} x\right)$ to $3.5$ units, we need to multiply it by $3.5$ to obtain $\green{3.5\cos\left(\dfrac{2}{3} x\right)}$.

$\qquad$[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: A graph of two trigonometric waves on an x y coordinate plane. The x and y axes scale by one. One wave is dashed and the other is solid. The maximum parts of the dashed graph are at (negative two pi, one), (zero, one), and (two pi, one). The minimum parts of the dashed graph are at (pi, negative one), (negative pi, negative one), (three pi, negative one), and (negative three pi, negative one). There is a point at (zero, one) and at (pi, negative one) on the dashed wave. The maximum parts of the solid graph are at (negative three pi, three and one half), (zero, three and one half), and (three pi, three and one half). The minimum parts of the solid graph are at (negative two pi, two) and (two pi, two). There is a point at (zero, three and one half) and at (three pi over two, negative three and one half) on the solid wave.

hints.content:
Now let's use a translation to bring the maximum point from $(0,3.5)$ to the location given by the graph, $(-2\pi,3)$.

This calls for a translation by $\red{2\pi}$ units to the left and $\purple{0.5}$ units down, so $3.5\cos\left(\dfrac{2}{3} x\right)$ is transformed into $3.5\cos\left(\dfrac{2}{3}(x\red{+2\pi})\right)\purple{-0.5}=3.5\cos\left(\dfrac{2}{3} x+\dfrac{4\pi}{3}\right)-0.5$.

To sum it up, this is a formula for $h(x)$:

$\qquad 3.5\cos\left(\dfrac{2}{3} x+\dfrac{4\pi}{3}\right)-0.5$
